name: Purplish Pink
lede: Purplish pink is a descriptive name, not a pigment or a place: a pink pulled toward purple, used by dictionaries for a whole run of older, more specific names.

sections.title: A description that stands in for names
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary uses the phrase as a definition for at least five entries: corinthian pink, fuchsia pink, mauvette, peach-blossom, and rose marie (which Paterson glosses as a deep pink or purplish pink) [1]. It also allows that orchid pink can be a purplish pink [1]. The books read do not treat the phrase as a color name of its own, only as the plain words that explain other names [1].

That is useful to know when you meet it. Where a name such as mauvette appears, the dictionary means a violet, a purple or a purplish pink, so the word covers a range, not one point [1]. See [[mauvette]], [[orchid-pink]] and [[rose-pink]] for the named neighbors.

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch here is a modern list color, recorded in the xkcd color survey of 2010 and built from the grammar purplish plus pink [2]. Its nearest ISCC-NBS name, from the 1955 system, is deep purplish pink, about seven units away [2]. In hue it sits on the cool side of [[pink]], toward [[magenta]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, none holds this color over at least five per cent of the canvas, and a finer within-painting search finds it in one [3]. It is rarer than 86 per cent of the named colors [3]. Photographs of aged, varnished paintings are the evidence here, so this says little about what painters mixed [3].
